chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Jaʿfar, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, that he said:
There is no harm in the droppings of chickens and pigeons affecting the garment.

key_terms.بِخُرْءِ: With the droppings or excrement of
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm or objection; a formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Does chicken or pigeon droppings on clothing affect ritual purity or salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity, stating that the droppings of chickens and pigeons on one's garment are not problematic. It is relevant to fiqh discussions on najasah and the validity of salat (prayer) when such substances come into contact with clothing.
